title: Review placement and Native KaTeX ownership repair

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Accepted ownership and evaluation-presentation operating model.

allowedWork: Review placement, shell, responsive lifecycle, and focused exact-state evidence.
Native KaTeX rendered-scene endpoint handles, hierarchical ownership views, equivalent-pose seam certificates, and per-leaf diagnostics.
Common-denominator pressure integration and focused deterministic verification through its human checkpoint.
disallowedWork: Evaluation-family exemplar implementation or default promotion.
Fraction-equivalence promotion, second-caller promotion, like-denominator arithmetic, or unrelated catalogue work.
Changes to semantic endpoints, approved fraction-equivalence choreography, public layouts, or user-owned dirty files.
goal: Relocate Catalogue Review, establish immutable shared Native KaTeX endpoint ownership, repair the common-denominator composite-to-leaf seam, and stop for human review.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified rollback unit with exact path staging and its completed Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: The Review change requires restructuring the Catalogue layout.
Shared endpoint handles alter settled KaTeX output or accessibility markup.
The repair changes mathematical endpoints, semantic identity, or approved fraction-equivalence choreography.
A seam can pass only through caller-local timing, opacity, offsets, or DOM rebinding.
Direct seek, reverse, font invalidation, or resize requires replay.
Work expands into evaluation presentation or family promotion before the human checkpoint.
Unrelated user work would need to be overwritten or reformatted.
Slice r22 reaches the mandatory human visual checkpoint.
